b_records.quote: If p1 ≥ p2 and q2 ≥ q1, then T1 ≥1 T2 (implying T1 ≥2 T2), because r is increasing. If p1 > p2 and q1 > q2, then the mode is a maximum and we can apply Theorem 2.2 of Ramos et al. (2000), recalling that E(Xi) = pi/(qi − 1), if qi > 1. Finally we obtain: p1 ≥ p2 and p1/(q1 − 1) ≥ p2/(q2 − 1) (with q1, q2 > 1) implies T1 ≥2 T2.

records.quote: Let X ~ N(µ1, σ1) and Y ~ N(µ2, σ2). Then, Xi:n and Yj:m have BG-normal distributions. According to Table 1, if µ1 ≥ µ2 and σ1 ≤ σ2, we can apply Theorem 3. For instance, let n = 35, m = 30 and j = 20. The minimum rank i such that Xi:35 ≥2 Y20:30 is given by i = max{j, ⌈nj/m⌉} = 24, where ⌈·⌉ denotes the ceiling function (Xi:35 ≥2 Y20:30 for i ≥ 24).

Table 1: SSD sufficient conditions for various BG families satisfying p1 ≥ p2 and p1/(q1 − 1) ≥ p2/(q2 − 1). GB1 (power baseline): a1 ≥ a2, b1 ≥ b2; GB2 (log-logistic): a2 ≥ a1 > 1, b1 ≥ b2; BG-Pareto: a2 ≥ a1 > 1, b1 ≥ b2; BG-uniform: a1 ≥ a2, b1 ≥ b2; BG-normal: µ1 ≥ µ2, σ1 ≤ σ2; BG-logistic: µ1 ≥ µ2, σ1 ≤ σ2.
records.family: GB1, GB2, BG-Pareto, BG-uniform, BG-normal, BG-logistic
